rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a material drafting template: both are presidential letters to congressional leaders seeking special legislation so a specifically named individual can serve on a federal board without adverse consequences under otherwise applicable law; both explain the individual's contemplated board role, describe the proposed statutory accommodation, and transmit a draft bill while requesting prompt congressional action. C03 and C23 share requests for legislation but lack this distinctive named-appointee-plus-statutory-exemption machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I therefore earnestly hope that the Congress will enact appropriate legislation which will exempt the position from the above-mentioned statutory restrictions. I enclose a draft of a proposed bill which would achieve this end.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am attaching hereto a draft of bill to authorize the President to appoint Major General Laurence S. Kuter as a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, without affecting his military status and perquisites.
shared_material.explanation: Both transmit draft legislation creating a tailored statutory accommodation necessary for a named individual to serve on a federal board.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also venture to hope that the Congress will agree with me that Mr. Acheson fulfills these requirements, and will therefore understand my desire to reappoint him to the position of civilian member and chairman.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I contemplate designating Major General Kuter as Chairman of the Board.
shared_material.explanation: Each letter centers the requested bill on the President's plan to place a named person in a board chairmanship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the problem which arises is broader than the appointment of any particular individual and will continue to be a serious impediment in the filling of this position
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The draft of bill would provide that Major General Kuter would continue, while serving as a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, to receive his military pay and allowances ... but ... would be subject to no supervision or control by the Department of the Air Force
shared_material.explanation: Both explain why ordinary legal rules impede the contemplated appointment and specify legislation that removes the impediment while preserving the intended institutional role.
